items.title: Archive
items.note: Archive closes the scope first, revokes and verifies every credential, then says archived; an unfinished archive stays executing and the tick finishes it; transitions through one guarded function; local, fault table and staging (Run 5.4: both tokens refused, both accessors 400 on the host).

items.title: Reactivate
items.note: Reactivation reads only: machine policy and token role against the digest, names against the index, every credential revoked and each accessor 400; a failure changes nothing (503, rejected); no token comes back; local and staging (Run 5.4: old tokens still 401, a new token resolves).

items.title: No deletion
items.note: Projects and environments as replayable operations, keyset lists, readiness; a pending environment cannot issue credentials is proven at the state gate and again on the real route by Run 5.1 (product code, real stores).

items.title: Values
items.note: Values: empty, 64 KiB of multibyte text, CR/LF/tab, four-byte characters stored exactly; oversize, NUL and lone surrogates refused before any effect and never echoed (product code, real stores; staging create).

items.title: Metadata
items.note: Metadata from the index: pages under a signed cursor with the metadata generation, bytewise order, literal prefixes, deleted and in-review names with their state; never OpenBao, never a value (product code, real stores).

items.title: Reveal
items.note: Masked until an explicit Reveal; the value is held only by the displaying component and is gone after 30 s, on hide, on a change of address and at sign-out; no secret-bearing route goes through the query cache (D-60). Local browser proof over real OpenBao; a historical version's reveal is Run 7.5's and the storage scan Run 7.10's.

items.title: Copy
items.note: Copy is an explicit button; the page then says the clipboard is outside MyKey and the copy cannot be taken back; no value in a notice or an error text.

items.title: Create
items.note: Create through the six-step protocol: one version carrying the operation id, index, version event, audit intent and success; replay, races on two processes, authorization and state refusals (product code, real stores; staging through the public name).

items.title: Update
items.note: Update with expected version and state tag: version_conflict with details, backend moved underneath goes to review, capacity 507, admission recheck (product code, real stores; staging through the public name).

items.title: History
items.note: History: OpenBao metadata joined with version events — who wrote each version and its last delete or undelete, twenty at most, no value; delete/undelete/restore made by the fixture until Run 4.4 adds their routes (product code, real stores).

items.title: Soft-delete
items.note: Soft delete of the current version under the protocol: state deleted, new tag, byte count kept, counters reduced; reveal, update and create refused after it; replay, races and a delayed answer (product code, real stores; staging with Run 4.5).

items.title: Undelete
items.note: Undelete brings the same version back with a new tag and equal digest; capacity from the kept byte count before any effect (product code, real stores).

items.title: Restore version
items.note: Restore writes an older version as a new one with cas = current, also over a deleted current; deleted or trimmed sources are 409; the source value appears in no database row (product code, real stores).

items.title: Concurrency
items.note: Concurrency with uncertain outcomes: the stale-work sweep moves executing operations to uncertain and accepted ones to rejected, one audit row each under two sweepers; a swept executor can neither finalize nor dispatch; the slot blocks the environment until settled (product code, real stores).

items.title: Unknown result
items.note: Unknown result: a landed write is reconciled as success without exclusion; a not-landed write is rejected only after executor exclusion; deletes and undeletes always need exclusion; evidence conflicts can be closed as unknown (product code, real stores; staging drill).

items.title: No destruction interface
items.note: No route and no runtime client method destroys a version or deletes metadata (unit); the runtime policy is denied kv/destroy and metadata deletion on real OpenBao (authority matrix, Run 2.1).

items.title: Format v1
items.note: Strict parser and canonical writer for format v1, with accepted and rejected fixtures and the rule and line of every rejection. Not yet wired to the import and export routes.

items.title: Loader compatibility
items.note: Canonical output checked with pinned @next/env and python-dotenv on a 65-case corpus; no value changed without a warning by key name. The export screen that shows the warnings is still to come.

items.title: Preview
items.note: Import preview: classification under the lock, values compared in memory only, nothing written; stored rows hold names, lines, classifications, versions and tags (product code, real stores).

items.title: Apply
items.note: Import apply and resume entry by entry through the mutation protocol; seven outcomes; partial when not every entry applied; resume never writes an entry twice.

items.title: Export
items.note: Export of an environment as a dotenv attachment: complete read under the lock, secret.export audited before the bytes, exact headers, no compression through the edge; 1,000 names of 7 MiB in at most 19.8 s on staging.

items.title: Round trip
items.note: Codec level only, and only within the 1 MiB import limit: serialise then parse reproduces names and values exactly in property tests. An environment may hold 8 MiB of values, so a large export is refused on re-import today. The export and re-import of a real environment is still to come.

items.title: Issue
items.note: Issuance with a marker under the environment's lock: issuer session, credential issuing + operation executing committed before the one create, the token checked and delivered only after accessor, expiry and active are committed; failures after the marker deliver nothing.

items.title: Native scope
items.note: A product-issued token used directly against OpenBao: read and list of its own path and lookup-self only; every write, delete, other scope, token create, renew and system path denied with a root control; lookup-self answers in another namespace with the token's own record (finding, nothing readable).

items.title: Inventory
items.note: The token is shown once in the 201; the inventory lists the catalog's view newest first with no accessor or token; no token bytes in PostgreSQL, logs, audit, jobs or OpenBao's audit device.

items.title: Revoke
items.note: Revocation denied in the product first (revoking committed before OpenBao is asked) and called revoked only after a lookup proved the token gone; an unproven revocation stays revoking and a new request finishes it; local, fault table and staging.

items.title: Uncertain/lost issuance
items.note: An unknown issuance blocks the environment until the sweep and ops reconcile-credentials revoke every unrecorded token and settle it (with executor exclusion when its token was not found); replay never returns a token; the lost-delivery procedure in machine-credentials.md; staging drill.

items.title: Machine routes
items.note: Machine keys and resolve: bearer authentication by lookup-self with the presented token, the catalog row and the path's own scope; reads made with the token itself; a dead token mid-read is 401 and closes nothing; current values only; local and on staging through the public name.

items.title: Residual
items.note: The residual asserted as it is: an older undeleted version answers 200 directly in OpenBao with the machine token, no product request returns it; written in machine-credentials.md and D-42.

items.title: Credential input
items.note: One token source (SECRETS_MACHINE_TOKEN or --token-stdin for keys/export), never a flag or argument; two or none are usage errors; no output repeats the token; Linux container evidence (four platforms in Run 5.7).

items.title: keys
items.note: secrets keys prints the live names only after the whole answer passed the validator; the CLI's client against the real API (digests equal the owner's export); Linux evidence.

items.title: run
items.note: run: the complete validated set before the spawn, no SECRETS_* in the child, collisions refused without --override, size checked, no shell, stdin to the child, signals forwarded once (terminal and not), status preserved; Linux container and staging; macOS not proven (the matrix's macOS jobs failed on the suite's test certificates and did not run again: cli-matrix.md).

items.title: Failure
items.note: 21 damaged or refused answers each launch nothing with their exit code and leave HOME, TMPDIR, XDG_* and the working directory empty; a signal before the spawn starts nothing; after revocation on staging run exits 77 and starts nothing.

items.title: export
items.note: export: one new 0600 file (O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, no chmod) whose parsed digests are the set, or nothing; links, existing paths and group-writable directories refused; cleanup only of the file it created; Linux container and staging.

items.title: Platforms
items.note: cli-v0.1.1 proven from the release on Linux x64 and arm64 and macOS x64 and arm64: project cli 53/53 on each (run 43857539084).

items.title: Contract
items.note: OpenAPI 3.1 from the runtime schemas, served reduced to the handled routes (each reaches a handler); breaking changes against baseline-v1.json fail contracts:check. The auth-route inventory is Session 3's auth:contract:check.

items.title: No passthrough
items.note: OpenBao-shaped aliases, method override, X-Vault-Token and X-Vault-Namespace reach no handler and no OpenBao audit entry; the document lists no token administration.

items.title: Reference
items.note: Document and read-only Scalar for a fully authenticated owner or admin; no execution, telemetry, CDN or third-party request in the captured browser session (D-45; Scalar kept).

items.title: Operator surface
items.note: Durable organization provisioning, provisioner process, drift sweep and review alert; AC-1.09 drill on staging (product code, real stores; staging).

items.title: Coverage
items.note: Audit coverage is a table checked both ways; one journey leaves a row for every action whose writer exists (PENDING_WRITERS for Runs 6.2-6.9); api rows carry their response's request id.

items.title: Backend audit
items.note: OpenBao's audit device is part of readiness: an audited call per 15 s; audit_failing opened, delivered and resolved on staging (alerts.md).

items.title: Audit view
items.note: Owners and admins read the tenant trail and current members' account rows; no foreign, global or anonymous row; filters, stable keyset pages, bound cursors; invalid details served empty and logged.

items.title: Correlation
items.note: The request id is the API's own and is on every audit row of a request; an incoming x-request-id is neither echoed nor logged; activity items carry the operation's current state.

items.title: Limits
items.note: Rate limits as pipeline steps (source before the body, session, credential, reveal/import/export/issue per person, machine misses per source); 429 with retry-after; a counter that cannot be written is 503; across two processes; locally.

items.title: Disk pressure
items.note: Disk pressure: 507 {limit: disk} on expanding mutations, reduction and sign-in continue, no record 503, real exhaustion 503 without value; locally and on staging (limits.staging.test.ts).

items.title: Health
items.note: Health, readiness and heartbeat v2 with twelve checks; unknown is not healthy; every condition drilled on staging (alerts.md).

items.title: Alerts
items.note: Fifteen alert conditions, each opened, delivered on the real Telegram channel and resolved on staging; a test alert on demand; detection from outside the host.

items.title: Auto-unseal
items.note: Unattended unseal from OVHcloud KMS on staging after restart, cold start and reboot; KMS outages behave as documented. Production at its first OpenBao start.

items.title: Certificate recovery
items.note: KMS certificate replaced without the old one on staging.

items.title: Paired backup
items.note: The daily pair on staging: writing closed by a trigger, captured, uploaded, read back, checked, signed and eligible by its own unit; 40 local captures under load restored whole.

items.title: Restore quarantine
items.note: A restore ends closed + verifying: gate v2 binds host, incarnation and build; the public listener is quarantined at every step a restore can stop at; gate open needs a fresh, complete report and re-checks it (local proof; the drill in Run 6.8).

items.title: Access revalidation
items.note: Access is revalidated by class: sessions, reset tokens, verifications deleted, accounts recovery_pending, credentials revoked, every accessor in every namespace revoked, AppRole secret ids rotated; nine old credentials each refused after a local restore.

items.title: Measurements
items.note: restoreMeasurements records capture time, age at restore, restore and revalidation time and result; host.ts writes them beside the report. Measured values, never an SLA.

items.title: Staging
items.note: Staging is a separate host built by the same tool and files as production.

items.title: Transport
items.note: Every hop that exists in Session 2 is verified TLS; OpenBao added in Run 2.7.

items.title: Host boundary
items.note: Host boundary on both hosts: default-deny firewall, VPN-only SSH, restricted containers.

items.title: Supply chain
items.note: A host release is built once on a clean clone: three images with the commit's build id, no npm/npx/corepack, scanned as the archives that ship (history, dependencies, images); release.json and SHA256SUMS only after every scan passes; published as host-vX.Y.Z (D-57).

items.title: Runbooks/upgrades
items.note: host.ts deploy promotes a release through the closed gate with the owner's journey and a deploy report, resumes a stopped deploy, and rolls back by deploying the previous release; staging converted to gate v2 and went forward, back and forward again (deploy.staging.test.ts); runbook deploy.md.

items.title: Honest use
items.note: docs/runbooks/known-limits.md: what the service does not do, each with where it was measured or decided; one runbook section per probe condition (alerts.md).

items.title: Browser protection
items.note: Every cookie-authenticated change needs this origin on every route and auth path that is not a GET; no GET changes a row; the page and every asset carry the content policy; injected inline and third-party scripts and framing are refused by Chromium. Local proof.

items.title: Fresh verification
items.note: One validity decision for sessions, atomic password change, fresh TOTP for the sensitive starts; AC-1.35 for export and issuance on stub handlers (product code, real stores).

items.title: Retention/key custody
items.note: Retention keeps the newest eligible pair always, deletes expired and released pairs verified and in order (eligible.json, row, bundle); the unit runs on staging; key readability probed on the KMS.

items.title: Connection
items.note: HTTP URL, untrusted/other-host/expired certificates, unsafe runtime settings, redirects and another API major each fail with their exit code before any credential is sent; Linux evidence (AC-1.37 on the four runners in Run 5.7).

items.title: Secret-free diagnostics
items.note: Canary sweep over the API, PostgreSQL and OpenBao logs, audit rows and error bodies, with controls; log fields checked by format; no diagnostic flags; core dumps off.

items.title: Audit integrity/retention
items.note: Chained audit segments (closed UTC days, rotated OpenBao files) read back from R2 before verified_at; late rows archived once; audit.purge_archived() the only delete, whole verified days 365 days old; locally and on staging.

items.title: Durable operation lifecycle
items.note: Durable operation lifecycle under crashes: accepted rows swept to rejected, executing rows to uncertain, settled by the operator; replays tell the truth at every stage (product code, real stores).

items.title: Replay contract
items.note: Replay contract under faults: the original key answers 202, then 503 outcome_unknown or the stored error, then the settled result; eight repeats during a held request change nothing (product code, real stores).

items.title: Complete read
items.note: Complete environment read under the lock: every live value of one generation or nothing; drift, review, slots, size, generation change and audit failure refuse the whole read (product code, real stores).

items.title: Setup/rotation
items.note: Setup and rotation from consumer-local.md and consumer-deploy.md, every block rehearsed against staging from a clean machine and a Docker host, both fixtures; no token in history, arguments, images, inspect, tree or output.

items.title: Human recovery after restore
items.note: Human recovery: the operator's mfa reset, then enrolment, sign-in, reveal digest and a refused change through the verification listener; the owner can do what an owner can after opening, and no more.

items.title: Restore readiness
items.note: Restore readiness: host.ts restore and restore-verify with runbook restore.md; refusals before anything is written (data present, KMS key unusable, unknown role in globals.sql); a stopped restore completes from step 1.

items.title: Reconciliation
items.note: Reconciliation: ops operations, reconcile-operation and reconcile-environment; an environment's index rebuilt from OpenBao (300 names within 60 s), a review ended, refused while an operation is unresolved or the lock is held (product code, real stores).

items.title: Owner information architecture
items.note: Every owner screen is reached from the navigation after a complete sign-in and shows the server's states in the server's words; no placeholder screen is left. Local browser proof.

items.title: Project and environment overview
items.note: The overview route and screen: names, immutable ids, state, review reason, last change and the index's key counts with source and time; a count that was not made is null and reads "not available". Local browser and integration proof; the staging demonstration is the gate's.

items.title: Credential understanding
items.note: The credentials screen and credentials.summary: name, scope, effective expiry, issuer, state, last use only when known, the seven-day warning as text, the token once through the forgetting holder, the lost-delivery explanation, revocation by typed name and fixed replacement guidance. Local browser proof over real OpenBao; the staging demonstration is the gate's.

items.title: Operation and activity timeline
items.note: The operations screen and the activity timeline: paged, scoped, the server's seven states by their own word, an uncertain operation never called failed, the operator sentence with the runbook's name, and nothing on the screens that reconciles. Local browser proof over real OpenBao.

items.title: Actionable cross-surface errors
items.note: One table maps every code to what happened, the safe next step and the ids; the nine failure classes each show their own words in a real screen, never the code or the server's text; an unknown outcome never invites a second send. Five classes by the server's own answer, four answered by the harness with the contract's envelope.

items.title: Truthful, useful product-local measurements
items.note: metrics.get and the overview's summary: outcomes by day, credentials by state and operations without an end, each with source, window and observation time; a day not measured is a null and reads "not measured", never zero; members are refused by the server. Local proof.

items.title: Private operator status
items.note: The private operator status view (host.ts status), every line with its observation time; no diagnostic route on the API (status.staging.test.ts).

items.title: Interaction quality
items.note: Labels on every control, errors tied to fields, Tab in reading order with a visible focus ring, dialogs that hold and return the focus, typed-name confirmation, words beside every colour, and no sideways movement at 360 pixels. Chromium only; no conformance to a standard is claimed.
